Cinematic Brand Film (TV-Style Spot).definition: A polished, agency-grade commercial with no one talking to camera: it opens on a striking cinematic shot (location, model or CGI product), cuts through a music-led montage of styled lifestyle, macro texture or CGI product shots (often one short feature super per shot), and closes on a logo/wordmark or offer end card.
Cinematic Brand Film (TV-Style Spot).why: Sells a premium mood and perceived brand size instead of an argument, so it lifts trust and price tolerance for aesthetic or giftable products, especially to warm-ish audiences and as a retargeting/brand layer.
how: Pick one setting/mood that matches the buyer's aspiration (rainy city, golden-hour beach, moody studio) or render the product in CGI.
Shoot 8-12 slow, well-lit shots: product hero, macro textures, hands/model using it; add one 2-4 word benefit super per shot, no voiceover.
Cut to a licensed music track and end on a clean logo + offer card.
Cinematic Brand Film (TV-Style Spot).closest_existing: Satisfying B-roll (Front-Splice) / Product Demo Ads: those buy attention or show function; this is a whole wordless TV-style brand spot selling mood and premium perception.
Cinematic Brand Film (TV-Style Spot).unviewed_ids_note: Remaining ~65 weaker candidates (mostly Big Joe/Rowen/EBC/Sol de Janeiro/Paul Rich F6-F7 dups) not viewed; defs match the format but unverified.

Brand Anthem Montage (Manifesto).definition: A cinematic manifesto: opens on a bold logo or one-word line, then a fast montage of many aspirational people/moments (or one protagonist in vignettes) runs under a single VO or word-by-word super that states what the brand believes, and closes on logo + tagline.
Brand Anthem Montage (Manifesto).why: Turns a commodity into an identity ('people like us use this'), building brand recall and a tribe; best for cold reach and to give the brand a point of view.
how: Write a 4-8 line belief statement about the buyer's identity, not the product (e.g. 'Your body needs it to perform, to recover, to embrace the moments').
Cut 10-15 short, high-energy lifestyle/athlete clips (stock or shot), one line of the manifesto per clip as a centered super or VO.
Show the product only in 1-2 beats, end on logo + tagline.
Brand Anthem Montage (Manifesto).closest_existing: Goal / Dream Journey or Personal Story: those follow one real person's arc; this is a belief statement read over a montage of many people.

Cinematic Mini-Film (Brand Short Story).definition: A 10-40s film-style micro story with a character, a setting and a small plot (a bellhop loads the bag, a man hunts the sea for his underwear, a kid's fingerprint becomes mom's necklace): the product is a prop inside the scene, there is no pitch or VO, and it ends on a title-card style logo.
Cinematic Mini-Film (Brand Short Story).why: Feels like a film scene, not an ad, so it earns attention and brand intrigue; works for fashion, gifting and lifestyle products with a strong aesthetic.
how: Write a 3-beat scene (setup, small twist/action, payoff) where the product is the object the character wants or uses.
Shoot it like cinema: one location, styled cast, slow camera, natural sound or one music cue, no talking to camera.
End on a title card with the brand name (like a film title) instead of a hard offer.
Cinematic Mini-Film (Brand Short Story).closest_existing: Scenarios / Day In The Life: those are creator-native or hypothetical; this is a scripted cinematic scene with a micro plot and a film title-card close.

Celebrity Spokesperson Spot.definition: A real famous person fronts the ad as the brand's spokesperson: opens on the celebrity's face/name delivering the hook to camera (selfie-style or studio), intercuts product close-ups and demo b-roll with kinetic claim supers while they keep talking, and closes back on them with a sign-off + logo/shop card.
Celebrity Spokesperson Spot.why: The face stops the scroll and transfers trust/status instantly; works when a recognizable person (even a niche micro-celebrity or known pro) can credibly endorse the product.
how: Book the most recognizable face your niche respects (micro-celebrity, known athlete/chef/creator) and have them open with their name or a personal hook.
Intercut their lines with 4-6 hero product/demo shots, each with one bold claim super.
Close on them saying a one-line endorsement, then logo + offer card.
Celebrity Spokesperson Spot.closest_existing: Celebrity Podcast Clip (Borrowed Authority): that borrows a real podcast clip; here the celebrity is hired and speaks directly as the brand's paid presenter.

Mini-Doc Portrait.definition: A cinematic 30s documentary vignette of one real, named person (athlete, mom, founder) with a name/title lower-third: they narrate their own life and routine in VO over observational footage, the product appears as part of that routine, and it closes on logo + tagline.
Mini-Doc Portrait.why: Feels like documentary truth rather than a testimonial pitch, so the claim rides on a real identity the viewer aspires to; great for supplements, fitness and performance products.
how: Find one real customer with an aspirational identity (triathlete, busy mom, fighter) and record a 2-min audio interview about their routine.
Shoot observational b-roll of their day (training, kitchen, family) with the product used naturally; add a name/title lower-third early.
Cut the best 5-6 VO lines over the footage with small captions, end on logo + tagline.
Mini-Doc Portrait.closest_existing: UGC Testimonial / Personal Story: those are selfie talk-to-camera; this is a produced observational doc with VO and a named lower-third.

Limited Collab Drop (IP Trailer).definition: A hype launch for a limited-edition product co-branded with a franchise or another brand: opens on the two logos locked up ('X x Y', 'Limited Edition'), shows the co-branded pack in the franchise's world with VFX/action beats and a quick product-in-use moment, and closes on a 'limited time only / before it's gone' scarcity card.
Limited Collab Drop (IP Trailer).why: Borrows a fandom's existing excitement and adds scarcity, so it pulls both fans and existing buyers into an urgent purchase; use for drops, seasonal editions and collabs.
how: Create a limited edition (collab with a creator/brand/local artist, or a seasonal theme) and design a co-branded pack.
Open on the 'X x Y Limited Edition' lockup, then 3-5 dramatic VFX/themed shots of the pack plus one quick use shot.
Close on 'Limited time only - gone when it's gone' with the shop link.
Limited Collab Drop (IP Trailer).closest_existing: Reaction / Trend-Hijack (Borrowed Fame): that disguises borrowed attention as native content; this is an official co-branded product launch trailer with a scarcity close.

Micro Bumper (2-6s).definition: An ultra-short 2-6s looping spot: one fixed headline or offer line sits on screen the whole time ('An icon of play. Rarely in stock.', 'the dreamiest sleepsuits for just £20') over 1-4 rapid product-in-use shots, then a logo flash; no VO, no story.
Micro Bumper (2-6s).why: Costs almost nothing, loops for repeat views and hammers one message cheaply; ideal for frequency/retargeting and for testing headlines and offers fast.
how: Write one 5-8 word headline or price/offer line.
Grab 1-4 one-second clips of the product in use (or a hanger-swap of variants) and cut to 2-6s so it loops cleanly.
Keep the headline fixed on screen, add a logo flash at the end, run many headline variants.
Micro Bumper (2-6s).closest_existing: Satisfying B-roll (Front-Splice): that is a scroll-stopper spliced before a longer ad; this is the whole ad in under 6s with one fixed headline.
